title: Mood Stabilisers: Lithium, Valproate, Carbamazepine, and Lamotrigine

steps.title: Lithium Therapeutic Monitoring
steps.tx: **Therapeutic drug monitoring of lithium** requires strict standardized trough blood sampling exactly 12 hours after the preceding nighttime dose once steady state is attained at four to five days. The therapeutic window for acute bipolar mania is 0.8 to 1.2 mEq/L, whereas maintenance therapy targets 0.6 to 0.8 mEq/L, because lithium exhibits an exceptionally narrow margin of safety.

steps.title: Chronic Lithium Adverse Effects
steps.tx: **Adverse sequelae of chronic lithium** therapy involve thyroid and renal function due to cellular accumulation. Inhibition of thyroid hormone synthesis causes primary hypothyroidism and goitre in up to 20 percent of patients. In the collecting ducts, lithium blunts aquaporin-2 expression, inducing nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with polyuria and polydipsia, which responds characteristically to the epithelial sodium channel blocker amiloride.

steps.title: Lithium Toxicity Presentation
steps.tx: **Severity grading of lithium toxicity** correlates directly with circulating serum concentrations: mild toxicity (1.5 to 2.0 mEq/L) causes coarse hand tremor, gastrointestinal nausea, diarrhoea, and mild ataxia. Moderate toxicity (2.0 to 2.5 mEq/L) produces hyperreflexia, muscular fasciculations, slurred dysarthric speech, and progressive confusion. Severe toxicity (>2.5 mEq/L) precipitates grand mal seizures, generalized myoclonus, cardiovascular collapse, and irreversible cerebellar damage.

steps.title: Emergency Management of Lithium Toxicity
steps.tx: **Hemodialysis indications in lithium poisoning** include any serum level exceeding 4.0 mEq/L regardless of symptoms, or any level surpassing 2.5 mEq/L accompanied by severe neurotoxicity, hemodynamic instability, or renal impairment. Because lithium is an uncharged single monovalent cation with negligible protein binding and a small volume of distribution, it is cleared with exquisite efficiency during hemodialysis.

steps.title: Sodium Valproate Pharmacology
steps.tx: **Pharmacological actions of sodium valproate** center on increasing central brain gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) concentrations through inhibition of GABA transaminase and succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase, alongside voltage-gated sodium channel blockade. Valproate serves as first-line therapy for acute bipolar mania, mixed affective states, and rapid cycling bipolar disorder, targeting serum trough concentrations between 50 and 100 micrograms per milliliter.

steps.title: Valproate Toxicity Profile
steps.tx: **Valproate teratogenicity and toxicities** encompass serious hepatic necrosis, acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis, dose-dependent thrombocytopenia, weight gain, and cosmetic alopecia. In utero exposure carries a 1 to 2 percent risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida and meningomyelocele, as well as congenital cardiac anomalies. Patients presenting with lethargy and vomiting must be evaluated for hyperammonemic encephalopathy, which is treated with oral L-carnitine.

steps.title: Carbamazepine Adverse Profile
steps.tx: **Adverse reactions to carbamazepine** include hepatic cytochrome P450 CYP3A4 auto-induction, necessitating upward dose titration after several weeks of initiation. Clinicians must screen for the HLA-B*1502 allele in populations of Asian ancestry to avert catastrophic Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Other classic adverse features include agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, hyponatremia due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, and cerebellar nystagmus.

steps.title: Lamotrigine Dosing and Rash
steps.tx: **Slow dose titration of lamotrigine** is mandatory when treating bipolar depression maintenance to avoid life-threatening mucocutaneous reactions. Concomitant sodium valproate inhibits lamotrigine glucuronidation, effectively doubling its elimination half-life and demanding that lamotrigine starting doses be halved. In contrast, enzyme inducers like carbamazepine accelerate lamotrigine clearance, requiring substantially higher maintenance doses.
